what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Memory loss of the sphere law in 2+1, with the referee's two openings. GIVEN (referee reports on four failed attempts): (1) the linear model DOES forget in the relevant sense: on the plane the transverse variance of a site grows like (3 sqrt 3/(4 pi)) sigma^2 log t (exact return sums), so the magnetization of the Gaussian approximation decays like a power; the conserved quantity is only the mean of the zero mode. (2) The twist route is alive: for a space-TIME twist field theta(x,t) the order-beta cost has minimum exactly 1/sum_{k<T} P_k, which tends to 0 by recurrence of the plane walk; attempts that used a twist static in level time found a cost Theta(T) and wrongly closed the route. (3) KL(vMF(k u) || vMF(k u')) = k A(k)(1 - u.u') exactly. TASK: prove m_t -> 0 on the infinite plane for every beta (block 26's open statement, PR #8170). Route A: the space-time twist: construct theta(x,t) = theta_0 g_T(x,t) with g built from the walk's Green function truncated at T, bound the path-space relative entropy by C beta theta_0^2/sum_{k<T}P_k, and conclude by the entropy inequality that the law of the record at the origin at level T is nearly invariant under rotation by theta_0. Route B: a lower bound on the growth of the transverse variance of the nonlinear law by comparison with the linear one. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/plane-memory-loss-2/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/plane-memory-loss-2/<name>/check.py"
